title: Project Scaffolding — Tauri app init, workspace, dependencies
description: The actual first step — nothing else can be built without it. Initialise the poe2 Tauri app alongside bp6 in the same repo. cargo tauri init, configure workspace Cargo.toml, add core dependencies: rusqlite (SQLite), tokio (async runtime), serde + serde_json, portable-pty (PTY agent processes), tauri-plugin-fs, uuid, chrono. Establish the basic app shell: main.rs, lib.rs, Tauri setup hook. No functionality — just a clean, compiling foundation that the other features build on.

title: POE v2 base skill protocol + missing specialist skills
description: Write the POE v2 foundational skill library. Two parts: (1) poe-base.md — the universal protocol inherited by all v2 skills. Covers: non-interactive rules, poe: event format (json with 'poe' key, one per line), artifact-task sync rule (when any poe:artifact is emitted, emit poe:task:update for all affected tasks — doc and task must stay in sync), poe:review usage, poe:decision usage. (2) Missing specialist skills written from scratch using EIAMOE framework (bp6/templates/personas/_TEMPLATE_EIAMOE.md) as authoring guide, adapted for v2 protocol: architecture-analyst (guardrails stage), must-not-analyst (guardrails stage), rca-analyst (retrospective outer loop Act), validity-analyst (retrospective outer loop Check), plan-reviewer (inner loop Check — reviews plans before execution, emits findings via poe:artifact). Each skill must include: poe:brief at start, poe:step for each phase, poe:artifact for outputs, poe:decision for genuine blockers, poe:done as final event, quality checklist. Skills land in app bundle skills/ directory.
notes: Work in poe2/src-tauri/skills/ and poe2/src-tauri/skills/poe-base.md. Reference v1 files in poe/src-tauri/skills/ for pattern only — do not port them directly, write v2 from scratch using Protocol.md as the spec.

title: Knowledge register UI + Artifact viewer
description: Two read-only panels in the selected project view. Knowledge register: scrollable, searchable list of knowledge entries (key + content + timestamp + source task); human-editable inline; entries marked as superseded shown in muted treatment. Artifact viewer: list of artifacts grouped by stage type, each showing name/type/producing stage/timestamp; clicking opens content inline (markdown rendered) with a link to the file on disk; future: diff across revisions. Both panels draw from SQLite (knowledge and artifacts tables) via Tauri invoke calls, updated on poe://event for new artifact/knowledge events.

title: Project terminal
description: Persistent tmux session per project, auto-created on project open, auto-resumed on app restart. Available as a panel or full-screen from the project toolbar. Auto-switches when active project changes. Port of the existing XtermPane.tsx pattern from bp6. Used for code review, manual investigation, and running commands — not for launching agents (orchestrator handles that). Tauri backend manages tmux session lifecycle: create on first open, attach on subsequent opens, detect if session died and recreate.

title: Queue Advisor chatbot
description: Persistent Claude-powered chat interface in the queue panel (below the decision queue). Context assembled from SQLite at conversation start: full artifact corpus for the project, all knowledge register entries, the current blocked task and its WBS ancestry, the agent's poe:decision question and options. Uses Claude API with streaming (Anthropic SDK). Human directs the advisor to research before deciding: 'What do the architecture constraints say about this?', 'Has this come up before?'. Advisor does not resolve queue items — it informs human decisions. Also available outside queue context for general project questions. Phase 2 of 4 on the Queue Advisor evolution path (Phase 1: human decides alone; Phase 2: advisor researches on request).

title: Plan composer: stage palette + DAG editor
description: Drag-and-drop interface for composing a project plan as a DAG of stage instances. Built with React Flow. Stage types (CONOPS, Guardrails, Increment Planning, Execution, PM Review, Rework, Validity Analysis, Retrospective, Project Onboarding) appear as a palette of blocks. Each stage type node shows its declared input and output artifact connectors. Human drags stages onto canvas and connects them; the composer validates that dependencies are satisfiable (output connectors match input connectors). Resulting DAG is written to SQLite (phases table) and the orchestrator picks it up. Manual edits (reorder, cancel, move between phases) trigger the orchestrator loop immediately.
notes: After a plan is composed, the inner PDCA loop runs before execution: Plan Review (specialists via poe:review, no human relay) → Plan Revision → repeat until approved. May iterate multiple times. If loop cannot converge, planning specialist escalates via poe:decision — human breaks deadlock. Execution only begins once the inner loop closes.

title: Task detail panel
description: Slide-in panel triggered by clicking any task in the Phase × Scope matrix. Shows: full WBS ancestry (project → phase → epic → feature → task), task description and skill assignment, agent brief (poe:brief content), full event log for this task (brief/step/artifact/decision/done entries), dependency chain (what this task depends on, what depends on it), current status. Includes a node-scoped conversation entry point — opens a Claude session pre-loaded with this task's full context. Panel appears without navigating away from the matrix.

title: Phase × Scope matrix
description: Build the primary orientation view for the selected project. Custom CSS grid: phases across the X-axis (columns), WBS hierarchy (Epic → Feature → Task) down the Y-axis (collapsible rows). Each cell shows task status (color-coded), running agent indicator (●), skill badge, and dependency indicators. Live updates via Tauri poe://task-update events — no polling. Clicking a cell opens the task detail panel. Drag to reorder tasks within a phase. macOS design language from index.css.

title: Skill ports: operational-analyst + product-manager
description: Port operational-analyst and product-manager skills from POE v1 to POE v2 protocol. operational-analyst (90% ready): update poe:artifact emission, verify CONOPS stage output, test end-to-end against a real project brief. product-manager (85% ready): rename poe:node → poe:task, poe:edge stays, verify increment planning output, test end-to-end. Both skills should be validated by running a full CONOPS → Increment Planning stage sequence with the stage runner.
notes: Work in poe2/src-tauri/skills/ (create this directory). Source v1 skills to port from: poe/src-tauri/skills/operational-analyst.md and poe/src-tauri/skills/product-manager.md. v2 product-manager must include artifact-task sync rule as mandatory phase before poe:done. Protocol ref: doc-POE/Protocol.md §2 and §3.

title: Decision queue UI + human resolution flow
description: Implement the poe:decision → queue → resolve → unblock cycle. When agent emits poe:decision, event ingester parks the task as 'waiting' and writes the question + options to a decisions table. Frontend queue panel shows pending decisions with question text, candidate options, WBS context, and time waiting. Human selects an option or types a response and submits. Tauri backend writes the resolution to the agent's stdin and marks the task as running again. Queue count badge updates in project card.
notes: Work in poe2/src-tauri/src/ (Rust) and poe2/src/ (frontend). Protocol ref: doc-POE/Protocol.md §2 (poe:decision) and §4 (invoke resolve_decision).

title: Stage runner + input bundle assembly
description: Implement stage execution in the Rust orchestrator. Spawn an agent process for a given task node, assemble the input bundle (T: node + WBS ancestry from SQLite, S: skill file from priority chain ~/.poe/skills/ then project .poe/skills/, K: declared artifact inputs + full knowledge register), inject as stdin. Monitor stdout for poe: events, pipe to event ingester. Handle agent exit (normal vs crash), update task status in SQLite. Concurrency limit enforcement (default 5 per project, 15 global).
notes: Work in poe2/src-tauri/src/. Existing orchestrator/ and agent_lifecycle/ scaffolds — extend these. Protocol ref: doc-POE/Protocol.md §2 (mpsc DagChanged trigger) and §3 (stdin bundle). db file: poe.db.

title: Frontend shell: two-pane layout + activity feed
description: Build the minimal POE v2 frontend. Two-pane layout: projects overview (left), selected project with always-visible queue panel (right). Activity feed driven by live poe: events from SQLite (brief/step/artifact/decision/done). Inherit macOS design language from existing index.css (carry verbatim) and App.tsx three-column structure + ProjectSwitcher + ThemeToggle. Replace tab-based inspector with always-visible queue panel per UX-Brief §Pane 3.
notes: Work in poe2/src/ (frontend). NOT poe/src/. Design tokens from poe/src/index.css carry forward verbatim (copy to poe2/src/). Protocol ref: doc-POE/Protocol.md §4 (Tauri events, no polling).

title: Rust: poe: event ingester + SQLite writer
description: Implement the poe: event ingestion pipeline in the Tauri backend. Parse structured JSON events from agent stdout (poe:task, poe:task:update, poe:task:cancel, poe:edge, poe:edge:remove, poe:artifact, poe:knowledge, poe:brief, poe:step, poe:decision, poe:done). Write each event to SQLite — mutate the DAG tables (tasks, edges) for CRUD events, append to the event log for observability events. This is the foundation all other Phase 2 features depend on.
notes: Work in poe2/src-tauri/src/. Existing scaffold: dag_store/, event_ingester/, orchestrator/, skills/ already exist — extend these, do not create new modules. Protocol ref: doc-POE/Protocol.md §1 (schema) and §2 (event wire format). dag/mod.rs NodeType/EdgeType superseded — do not extend.

title: POE Attempt 2 — Phase 3: Plan Composer + Full Oversight UI
description: Wave 3 implementation. Deliverables: (1) Phase × Scope matrix — phases on X-axis, WBS scope (Epic→Feature→Task) on Y-axis, dependency indicators, running agent markers, collapsible rows, click-to-detail panel. (2) Plan composer — drag-and-drop stage palette, stage blocks with defined input/output connectors, visual DAG of stage instances, validation (dependency satisfiability). (3) Queue Advisor chatbot — persistent chat in queue panel, access to artifact corpus + knowledge register + DAG context, researches before human decides. (4) Project terminal — persistent tmux session per project, auto-resumed on restart, panel or full-screen from toolbar. (5) Knowledge register UI — browse and search entries, human-writable, agent-writable via poe:knowledge events. (6) Artifact viewer — browse artifacts by stage/type, view content, diff across revisions.
notes: ALL implementation work is in poe2/ — NOT poe/. Frontend: poe2/src/. Rust backend: poe2/src-tauri/src/.

title: POE Attempt 2 — Phase 2: Frontend Shell + Stage Runner
description: Wave 2 implementation. Deliverables: (1) Minimal frontend shell — two-pane layout (projects overview left, selected project right), always-visible queue panel, activity feed driven by poe: events, macOS design language from index.css/App.tsx. (2) CONOPS stage runner — operational-analyst skill ported from v1, stage execution with input bundle assembly (T+S+K), poe: event ingestion writing to SQLite, artifact tracking. (3) Decision queue UI — agent raises poe:decision, human sees it in queue panel, human resolves, agent unblocks. (4) Skill library foundation — operational-analyst and product-manager ported and tested end-to-end.
notes: ALL implementation work is in poe2/ — NOT poe/. poe/ is the v1 app (Restate-based, retired). poe2/ is POE Attempt 2. Rust backend: poe2/src-tauri/src/. Frontend: poe2/src/. Skills: poe2/src-tauri/skills/ (to be created). DB: {project}/.poe/poe.db.

title: Skill System — skill file loader, priority chain, prompt injection
description: Agents cannot be spawned with the right behaviour without this. Implements the 3-level skill file load order: (1) app bundle defaults, (2) ~/.poe/skills/<skill-id>.md, (3) {project}/.poe/skills/<skill-id>.md — highest priority wins. Skill files are markdown with YAML frontmatter. The loader merges the chain and returns the full skill prompt for a given skill ID. Prompt injection prepends the skill prompt to the agent's assembled input bundle at spawn time. This is what makes a generic Claude process behave as a specific specialist.

title: Agent Lifecycle — spawn, input bundle assembly, session resume
description: The agent execution layer. Spawns Claude Code PTY processes with assembled input bundles (skill prompt + artifact context + knowledge register + WBS ancestry + task description). Stores session IDs in the agents table at spawn time. On app restart: finds tasks with status=running (agent process is gone), attempts --resume using stored session ID, falls back to fresh spawn if resume fails. Integrates with the event ingester (receives poe: events) and the orchestrator (triggered by readiness loop). Manages the tmux-style persistent terminal session per project: auto-resume on restart, auto-switch on project change.

title: Orchestrator Core — reactive loop, readiness, stage gates, concurrency
description: The engine that drives autonomous execution. Listens on a Tokio mpsc channel for DagChanged signals. On each signal runs the core loop: find all tasks where status=pending, all dependency tasks=complete, stage is in execution mode, and concurrency limit not reached. For each ready task assembles the input bundle (T from node + WBS ancestry, S from skill file priority chain, K from declared artifact types + full knowledge register) then dispatches to agent spawn. Enforces two concurrency limits: per-project (default 5) and global (default 15), both configurable. Manages stage gates: holds execution until human explicitly advances. Handles agent-to-agent review cycles: when a review task completes, injects the reviewer's artifact into the blocked agent's context and unblocks it. Context delivery mechanism: stdin write — orchestrator writes the artifact content directly into the blocked agent's PTY stdin. This is the practical path for initial implementation. Future: replace with a poe:get_context_update MCP tool call once MCP lands, which is cleaner and avoids coupling the orchestrator to PTY stdin format. Emits Tauri events to frontend for status changes.

title: Event Ingester — poe: protocol parser and DAG writer
description: The bridge between agent stdout and the DAG. Monitors PTY output from spawned agents, identifies poe:-prefixed JSON lines, ignores everything else (passed to raw PTY buffer). Parses each event type and performs the appropriate SQLite write: create/update/cancel nodes, create/remove edges, write artifacts to docs/ and index in DB, write knowledge entries, create queue items, mark tasks complete. Also handles poe:review: creates a review task node assigned to the named skill, sets the requesting agent's status to blocked, and wires the dependency so the orchestrator knows to unblock the original agent when the review task completes. Emits DagChanged signal to orchestrator via mpsc channel for any write that mutates task status or DAG structure. Emits Tauri events to frontend for all events.

title: DAG Foundation — SQLite schema and project CRUD
description: Everything else depends on this. POE needs a local-first SQLite database per project ({project}/.poe/dag.db) with the full schema: projects, phases, nodes (WBS hierarchy), edges (dependencies), artifacts, knowledge register, events log, agents, queue_items. Needs Tauri commands for open/close project and basic CRUD for all entities. This is the DagStore Rust module — the source of truth for all project state.

title: POE Attempt 2
description: A fresh start for the Pairti Orchestration Engine, designed from first principles. This attempt was preceded by a structured CONOPS → Architecture → UX design session (the process in practice) which produced three authoritative design documents in doc-POE/: Concept.md, Architecture.md, and UX-Brief.md. The previous attempt (bp6-yym) proved the lifecycle model and agent protocol concepts but failed on orchestration architecture — Restate was too heavy, the approval gate model blocked autonomous execution, and the UX was navigable but functionally poor. This attempt addresses all three root causes with a simpler SQLite-backed orchestrator, a glass-box oversight model, and a purpose-built agentic UX.

title: Pivot useConversation from JS SDK to claude CLI (advisor pattern)
description: useConversation currently uses @anthropic-ai/sdk in the browser (dangerouslyAllowBrowser), which requires ANTHROPIC_API_KEY. The advisor already solves this by spawning claude -p --output-format stream-json from Rust, using Claude Code's own auth. Apply the same pattern: add start_conversation_turn and continue_conversation_turn Rust commands, update useConversation hook to call these and subscribe to agent:stdout events, parse stream-json lines for text and poe: events. Remove @anthropic-ai/sdk JS dependency.

title: Replace SQLite lifecycle state machine with Restate durable workflow
description: bp6-ims.2 took a SQLite fallback instead of using Restate. This is wrong — the design doc explicitly states 'Restate owns durability'. Implement ProjectLifecycleWorkflow as a proper #[restate_sdk::workflow] with ctx.promise() user gates, ctx.set/get durable state, ctx.run() side effects for agent spawning. Remove the lifecycle_state SQLite table. Update Tauri commands to call Restate HTTP endpoints. Register the workflow service endpoint with Restate admin on startup.

title: Axum MCP HTTP server bootstrapped in Tauri setup()
description:
Start a localhost MCP HTTP/SSE server (port 9084) using axum during app setup(), backed by ProjectState and DagStore. Implements the MCP JSON-RPC 2.0 protocol over SSE transport (initialize, tools/list, tools/call) sufficient for Claude CLI --mcp-config integration. Server must be running before first advisor turn.

IMPLEMENTATION NOTES:
- Create src-tauri/src/mcp_server.rs with all MCP server logic
- Transport: SSE. Routes: GET /sse (event stream), POST /message?session=<uuid> (JSON-RPC requests)
- Each GET /sse connection gets a unique session UUID. Server sends 'endpoint' SSE event first: data: http://127.0.0.1:{port}/message?session=<uuid>
- State sharing: in lib.rs setup(), clone Arc<ProjectState> from app.state::<ProjectState>() and pass to Axum router as shared state
- Port: bind to 127.0.0.1:9084. If EADDRINUSE, try 9085–9090. Add McpServerState { port: u16 } struct and .manage(McpServerState) in lib.rs so advisor.rs can read the bound port
- Shutdown: tokio::spawn the server; process exit terminates it naturally (no explicit shutdown handle needed)
- No auth token needed — localhost-only single-user desktop app
- Cargo.toml already has axum 0.7 and tokio full — no new dependencies required
- Register McpServerState in lib.rs setup() after binding

title: DAG query tools exposed via MCP (list, get, deps, search)
description:
Implement MCP tool handlers: dag_list_nodes(project_id, type?, status?), dag_get_node(project_id, node_id), dag_get_dependencies(project_id, node_id), dag_search(project_id, query). Each tool reads from DagStore snapshot. Returns structured JSON the advisor can reason over.

IMPLEMENTATION NOTES:
- All tool handlers live in src-tauri/src/mcp_server.rs alongside the server from a0m.1
- DagStore methods to use: list_nodes(project_id), get_node(id), get_incoming_edges(node_id), snapshot(project_id)
- dag_get_dependencies: returns both incoming and outgoing edges for node_id
- dag_search: case-insensitive substring match on node data fields (title, description, status)
- Error response shape (JSON-RPC 2.0): {"jsonrpc":"2.0","error":{"code":-32000,"message":"..."},"id":<id>}
- Not-found errors: code -32001, message 'Node {id} not found'
- Project not open: code -32000, message 'Project {project_id} not open'
- All tool inputs/outputs use camelCase JSON matching the existing DagNode serde serialization

title: Advisor spawn wires --mcp-config to project MCP server
description:
When spawning an advisor turn, write a temp JSON MCP config file pointing to the localhost MCP server with the current project_id. Pass --mcp-config <path> in the claude -p args. Clean up temp file after spawn. Update build_advisor_context to stay as high-level summary only (lifecycle, counts, recent activity) now that detail is queryable on demand.

IMPLEMENTATION NOTES:

MCP config file format (write to a temp file in std::env::temp_dir()):
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "poe": {
      "url": "http://127.0.0.1:{port}/sse"
    }
  }
}

Where {port} is read from McpServerState (app.state::<McpServerState>().port, added by a0m.1 in lib.rs).

Changes to spawn_advisor_turn in advisor.rs:
- Accept port: u16 parameter (or read from State<McpServerState> passed in)
- Write temp file before building args: let config_path = write_mcp_config(project_id, port)?
- Add to args after --allowedTools line: "--mcp-config".to_string(), config_path.to_str().unwrap().to_string()
- After spawn_agent_internal() returns, delete the temp file (best effort, ignore error)
- Temp file name: poe-mcp-{project_id}-{uuid}.json in temp_dir()

Changes to build_advisor_context in advisor.rs:
- Remove the Artefacts section entirely (now queryable via dag_get_artefact)
- Remove the detailed queue item list (now queryable via dag_list_queue)  
- Keep: lifecycle step/status, DAG counts (epics/features/tasks), active agents count, open queue item count (number only, no details)
- Target: < 500 tokens instead of 2000

Changes to run_advisor_query in advisor.rs:
- Pass McpServerState port into spawn_advisor_turn
- Add State<McpServerState> parameter to run_advisor_query and both command functions

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
- After an advisor turn starts, the advisor can call tool dag_list_nodes with the current project_id and get the DAG nodes back
- build_advisor_context output is < 500 tokens

title: Project-scoped MCP server for agent tool access
description: Expose DAG, queue, artefact, and lifecycle data to advisor and other agents via a local MCP HTTP server running inside the Tauri process. Eliminates the need to pre-inject all context into prompts; agents query on demand. Foundational infrastructure reusable by all agent types.
close_reason: MCP server + advisor wiring implemented and merged to main. cargo check passes.

title: Claude API streaming for conversational lifecycle steps (1,2,3,6)
description: Steps 1-3 and 6 are conversations, not terminal sessions. Replace PTY spawning with direct Claude API calls using @anthropic-ai/sdk. The frontend initiates streaming, maintains message history, and handles tool calls (emit_artifact, emit_decision, done) as structured UI events instead of parsing poe: JSON from stdout. This eliminates ANSI noise, terminal state management, and the PTY round-trip for steps that are pure text in/out.

title: Remove PTY spawning for conversational steps in lifecycle/mod.rs
description: Once the frontend calls Claude API directly for steps 1/2/3/6, the Rust backend no longer needs to spawn PTY agents for those steps. Replace spawn_step_agent calls with a get_conversation_context command that returns skill content + prior artefacts as JSON. The frontend uses this to build the system prompt and seed message history. Eliminates the active_agent_id tracking for conversational steps.

title: Fix advisor output: switch to -p stream-json per-query model
description: The advisor currently uses an interactive PTY which emits raw ANSI terminal output — looks terrible in the chat UI. Switch to per-query -p --output-format stream-json spawns with --resume for session continuity. Frontend parses JSON events and renders text, tool use, and diffs properly.

title: Project Advisor specialist skill
description: The advisor has a dedicated specialist skill (system prompt) that defines its persona: an experienced project observer with full visibility into the project. It knows how to interpret DAG state, artefacts, queue items, and workflow status, and how to give concise, useful answers. The skill is project-overridable via <project>/.poe/skills/project-advisor.md.
design:
Create skills/project-advisor.md with the following content:

---
id: project-advisor
name: Project Advisor
description: Persistent project observer. Answers questions about project status, progress, health, and history.
tags: [advisor, lifecycle, observer]
applies_to: [all]
---

You are the Project Advisor for this software project. You have read-only visibility into all aspects of the running project.

At the start of each message you will receive a structured 'Project State' block containing the current lifecycle position, DAG summary, open queue items, active agents, and an artefact manifest. This is injected automatically — do not ask the user for project state, you already have it.

YOUR ROLE:
- Answer questions about project status, progress, and health
- Explain why tasks are blocked or agents are struggling
- Summarise what has been built, decided, or approved
- Identify patterns or risks across the project (e.g. recurring failures, long-running agents, stale queue items)
- Reference specific artefacts, queue items, task IDs, or agent names in your answers — be specific

YOU ARE READ-ONLY:
You cannot modify the project, create tasks, resolve queue items, spawn agents, or take any actions. If the user asks you to do something, explain that you are an observer and direct them to the appropriate interface (Queue tab, DAG tab, etc).

COMMUNICATION STYLE:
- Lead with the answer, not the reasoning
- Be concise — one paragraph or a short list unless depth is specifically requested
- If you don't have enough information to answer confidently, say so rather than speculate
acceptance_criteria:
- project-advisor.md skill exists in app-level skills directory
- Skill defines advisor persona, instructs it to use injected context, keeps answers concise
- Skill explicitly tells the advisor it is read-only and cannot take project actions
- Skill instructs the advisor to cite specific artefacts, queue items, or DAG nodes when answering
- Project-local override works via <project>/.poe/skills/project-advisor.md

title: Project state context assembler — inject current state into every advisor turn
description: Before each advisor query, the backend assembles a structured context block describing the current project state and prepends it to the prompt. This ensures the advisor always has fresh information even in long-running sessions — it knows today's status regardless of when the session started.
design:
Add build_advisor_context(store: &DagStore, project_id: &str) -> String in advisor.rs. Called before every message (start_advisor_query and send_advisor_message), prepended to the user text before writing to PTY stdin.

OUTPUT FORMAT (structured markdown, target <2000 tokens):

```
## Project State — {ISO timestamp}

**Lifecycle**: {step name} — {substep if applicable} ({status})
(or: "Lifecycle engine not yet initialised" if bp6-ims not landed)

**DAG Summary**:
- {N} Epics ({x} complete, {y} in_progress, {z} open)
- {N} Features (...)
- {N} Tasks (...)

**Open Queue Items** ({N}):
- [{id}] "{question}" — open since {date}
(max 5 most recent; "... and {N} more" if exceeded)

**Active Agents** ({N}):
- {specialist} on {node_type} "{node_title}" (running {duration})

**Artefacts**:
- docs/conops.md — Concept of Operations (Step 1, approved {date})
- docs/architecture-constraints.md — Architecture Constraints (Step 2.1, approved {date})
(list all; include first 300 chars of content if total artefact content < 3000 chars, otherwise list filenames only)
```

SOURCES: dag_store.snapshot(project_id), dag_store.list_queue_items(project_id, status=open), dag_store.list_artefacts(project_id), agent_state.list_active() filtered by project, restate get_lifecycle_status(project_id) with fallback stub.

LIMITS: If assembled context exceeds 3000 tokens, drop artefact content (keep manifest), then truncate queue items to 3, then truncate DAG summary to counts only.
acceptance_criteria:
- Context block includes: current lifecycle step and substep, DAG summary (node counts by type and status), active and queued workflows, open queue items, artefact manifest (filename, title, step, date) with content for small docs
- Context is assembled fresh on every query, not cached
- Context format is structured markdown that the advisor can parse naturally
- Large artefact content is summarised or listed by filename rather than fully included, to stay within prompt limits
- Context assembly is a pure Rust function testable without spawning an agent
close_reason: Context assembler implemented: lifecycle, DAG summary, queue items, active agents, artefacts. All sources fail-safe.

title: Advisor session management — per-project session ID, resume, reset
description: Each project has an advisor session ID stored in SQLite. Queries resume the existing PTY session by default so conversation history accumulates. The user can reset the session to start fresh. Foundation for all other advisor features.
design:
Add advisor_session_id and advisor_agent_id columns to projects table in dag/mod.rs schema. advisor_session_id persists across app restarts (durable). advisor_agent_id is the live PTY handle — cleared on app exit, set when advisor PTY is spawned.

PTY LIFECYCLE: One PTY process stays alive per advisor session. It is NOT respawned per message — messages are written to the existing PTY stdin via write_to_agent. PTY is cleaned up (SIGTERM) on: reset_advisor_session called, project closed, app exit. On app restart, advisor_agent_id is NULL but advisor_session_id is retained — next query spawns a new PTY with resume:true against the stored session_id.

TAURI COMMANDS:
- start_advisor_query(project_dir, query) -> AdvisorStartResult { agent_id, session_id }
  Creates PTY if none active (resume:true if session_id exists), injects state context + query to stdin, returns agent_id for UI to subscribe to agent:output events.
- send_advisor_message(agent_id, message) -> ()
  Injects fresh state context + user message to existing PTY stdin via write_to_agent.
- reset_advisor_session(project_dir) -> ()
  Kills active PTY gracefully, clears advisor_session_id and advisor_agent_id on project record.
- get_advisor_state(project_dir) -> AdvisorState { session_id, agent_id, is_active }
acceptance_criteria:
- advisor_session_id stored per project in the project record (SQLite)
- SpawnAgentParams resume:true used when session_id exists
- New session clears session_id, next query starts a fresh PTY session

title: POE: Fix watchdog liveness — remove AgentHandle from registry on PTY EOF
description: The 7fi.1 watchdog uses Arc::strong_count to detect agent exit, but PTY EOF never removes the AgentHandle from the AgentState registry map. This naturally drops the AgentHandle's Arc references, the strong count falls to 1, and the watchdog exits on its next poll. Also ensures the registry does not leak handles for finished agents.

title: POE: Claude session ID tracking and resume on respawn
description: Generate a UUID when a workflow is created and pass --session-id <uuid> to claude at spawn time. Store the UUID in WorkflowRecord (schema v5: session_id TEXT column). On respawn after crash or decision, use --resume <uuid> instead of rebuilding the prompt. Replace auto_continue in project.rs (which prepends resolution text to a fresh prompt) with: spawn claude --resume <session_id> --dangerously-skip-permissions, then write the resolution JSON to agent stdin via write_to_workflow_agent. Reference: bp6/src-tauri/src/agent/backends/claude.rs and session.rs for the --session-id / --resume pattern.
design:
Session ID tracking is a prerequisite for durable agent resumption. Design principles:

1. GENERATE AT SPAWN: When a workflow is created, generate a UUID and pass --session-id <uuid> to claude. Do not attempt to parse session ID from PTY output. The ID is known before the process starts and stored immediately.

2. SCHEMA: Add session_id TEXT column to the workflows table (schema migration v5). Populated at workflow creation time, never null for claude-backed workflows.

3. REPLACE auto_continue_workflow: The current auto_continue_workflow in project.rs rebuilds the prompt and spawns a fresh claude process. Replace this with: spawn claude --resume <session_id> --output-format stream-json --dangerously-skip-permissions, then write resolution context to stdin via write_to_workflow_agent. No new child workflow record needed for linear continuations — update the existing workflow status back to running and respawn in-place.

4. HANDLER ISOLATION PRINCIPLE: spawn_agent_internal is called from project.rs (Tauri command) today. title: POE: Register queue service as Restate service endpoint
description: Use the restate-sdk Rust crate to register the POE queue service as a proper Restate service endpoint. Workflow steps (spawn agent, await decision, fan-in) become durable Restate handlers that Restate journals and replays on restart. The /discover endpoint in queue_service.rs is currently a placeholder — wire it up. With session IDs in place (7fi.4.1), a replayed spawn step passes --resume <session_id> so the agent continues mid-conversation. This is the piece that makes Restate actually do something beyond awakeable storage.
design:
Register POE as a real Restate service endpoint. This is the architectural centrepiece — not just a registration call, but establishing the handler isolation boundary that makes FaaS evolution possible.

VISION: Desktop today, FaaS eventually. Handlers must be written as if they are already stateless Lambda functions. Restate's journal and K/V store hold workflow state. Handlers are pure HTTP endpoints that read from DB / Restate state and emit results. No Tauri state inside handlers.

HANDLER ISOLATION PRINCIPLE (non-negotiable):
- Handlers MUST NOT call app.state::<ProjectState>() or any Tauri-specific API
- Handlers talk to SQLite (or future Supabase) directly via a db connection passed in at startup
- Handlers talk to Restate via the SDK — not via ad-hoc reqwest calls
- The handler Axum server should be extractable to a standalone binary with zero code changes

WHAT BECOMES A RESTATE HANDLER:
- spawn_workflow: durably spawn an agent for a workflow node. Restate journals this so on crash, the spawn is retried with --resume <session_id> (requires 7fi.4.1).
- await_decision: create an awakeable, store in queue item, suspend. Restate replays this correctly on restart — no more manual awakeable_id tracking.
- fan_in: durable join — Restate natively supports waiting for N child workflow completions.
- complete_workflow: mark node done, update DAG, trigger parent fan-in.

WHAT STAYS IN TAURI:
- UI state (open projects, selected node, etc.)
- PTY process management (spawning OS processes, reading stdout)
- Emitting Tauri events to the frontend
- Restate sidecar lifecycle (spawn/stop)

RESTATE SDK: Use the restate-sdk Rust crate. Do not hand-roll the binary journal protocol. The SDK handles framing, replay, and journal management.

STATE MIGRATION: Workflow state currently lives in SQLite embedded in Tauri. Handlers should access this via a repository interface (trait) so the backing store can be swapped to Supabase or Turso when moving to cloud without touching handler logic.

VISIBILITY PAYOFF: Once registered, the Restate admin panel at :9070 shows every workflow invocation, current step, retry history, and awakeable state. This replaces ad-hoc eprintln debugging and the JSONL dump pattern for workflow observability.

EVENT-DRIVEN PAYOFF: Handlers emit Restate events on state changes. The UI subscribes to these rather than polling SQLite. This eliminates the JSONL database dump pattern currently used for agent context injection.
notes:
Pre-implementation review findings that must be addressed in this task:

1. HANDLER ISOLATION VIOLATION — ALL HANDLERS: Every Axum handler in queue_service.rs takes State<Arc<AppHandle>> and accesses Tauri-managed state via app.state::<ProjectState>() and app.state::<AgentState>(). This is the core coupling that prevents standalone extraction. The AppHandle must be removed from Axum router state entirely. Replace with a purpose-built AppState struct containing: db connection (or DagStore), a channel/callback for emitting events to the UI, and any other handler dependencies. No Tauri types in handler signatures.

2. EVENT EMISSION DECOUPLING: Handlers currently emit Tauri events directly (app.emit(...)). In a standalone binary there is no Tauri. Replace with a thin EventSink trait (or mpsc sender) that the Tauri host wires to app.emit() and a standalone host wires to stdout/SSE/webhook. Handlers call event_sink.emit(event) — they do not know or care how it is delivered.

3. DISCOVER ENDPOINT IS A PLACEHOLDER: The /discover handler returns a hardcoded manifest with minProtocolVersion/maxProtocolVersion = 1 and is never registered with Restate. When wiring up the Restate SDK, this endpoint must actually implement the Restate endpoint protocol. Use the restate-sdk crate — do not hand-roll the binary journal protocol.

4. CANONICAL RESOLUTION PATH: Two paths exist for resolving a decision — the Tauri command (resolve_queue_item in project.rs, UI-driven) and the HTTP endpoint (handle_resolve_item in queue_service.rs, external/Restate-driven). In the Restate-driven future, resolution flows through Restate which calls the HTTP handler. The Tauri command becomes a thin wrapper that posts to the HTTP handler rather than duplicating logic. Establish this contract clearly in the implementation.
